tagline: The world's highest seat of government fills a canyon at 3,600 metres, where cable cars float over brick neighbourhoods, cholita wrestlers perform and the Witches' Market sells llama fetuses for luck.
overview: Founded in 1548 in a deep Andean canyon, La Paz is the seat of Bolivia's government and, at over 3,600 metres, the highest capital city on Earth. The valley walls rise so steeply that Mi Teleférico — the world's largest urban cable-car network — became the main public transport.

The city is as strange as it is spectacular. The Witches' Market sells dried llama fetuses and charms for Pachamama rituals, the Moon Valley's eroded spires look lunar, and Sunday afternoons bring cholita wrestling — indigenous women in bowler hats fighting for the crowd.

The old centre keeps colonial churches, the curve of Jaén Street's museums and the towering San Francisco basilica. Adventures radiate outward: biking the 'Death Road' down the Yungas, climbing 6,000-metre Huayna Potosí, or crossing to Copacabana and Lake Titicaca.

funFacts.title: THE HIGHEST CAPITAL
funFacts.text: La Paz's government quarter sits at 3,640 metres — visitors feel the thin air on arrival.

funFacts.title: CABLE-CAR COMMUTING
funFacts.text: Mi Teleférico is the world's longest urban cable-car system, with 10 lines strung across the canyon.

funFacts.title: A MARKET OF MAGIC
funFacts.text: The Witches' Market sells charms, herbs and dried llama fetuses buried under homes for good fortune.

funFacts.title: THE DEATH ROAD
funFacts.text: The Yungas Road was once called the world's most dangerous — now it's a bucket-list downhill bike ride.

funFacts.title: THE OLDEST STREET
